message.content:
Below is a minimal **HTTP‑request** skeleton that will return *only* the `id` and `context` columns from the Historical WHOIS Details table for the name “domain6.xyz”, capped at eight rows and told explicitly to use the **Key Definition** (`key_def`) flag so that the response contains the column metadata rather than raw values.

> ⚠️ **NOTE:**  
> – Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your actual authentication token.  
> – Adjust the base URL (`https://api.yourprovider.com/…`) to match the real service host.  

---

### 1️⃣ Sample cURL Request

```bash
curl --silent \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
     --get \
     --data-urlencode "q=domain6.xyz" \          # Search term
     --data-urlencode "fields=id,context" \      # Only id + context
     --data-urlencode "limit=8" \                # Max 8 records
     --data-urlencode "key_def=true" \           # Return Key Definitions
     "https://api.yourprovider.com/v1/historical-whois/details"
```

#### What Each Parameter Does

| Param   | Value                     | Purpose |
|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `q`     | `domain6.xyz`             | Target search keyword (the domain).         |
| `fields`| `id,context`              | Tell the server to send back just those two columns. |
| `limit` | `8`                       | Cap the number of returned rows to 8.        |
| `key_def`| `true`                    | Instructs the API to embed the *column definition* block in the payload instead of plain text values. |

---

### 2️⃣ Expected Response Skeleton

If everything goes well, the API returns something along these lines:

```json
{
  "_meta": {
    "count": 5,
    "total_count": 12,
    "page_size": 8,
    ...
  },
  "columns": [
    { "name":"id","label":"Object ID","datatype":"string"},
    { "name":"context","label":"Context","datatype":"text"}
  ],
  "rows":[
    {"id":"obj_00123","context":"Historical record A..."},
    {"id":"obj_00456","context":"Historical record B..."},
    ... up to 8 entries max
  ]
}
```

Because `key_def=true`, the `"columns"` array gives you the exact schema mapping—useful when building UI tables or debugging downstream processing pipelines.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick One‑liner Alternative (JSON Body)

Some SDKs prefer sending a POST with a JSON body; here’s the equivalent:

```http
POST https://api.yourprovider.com/v1/historical-whois/details HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>

{
  "query": "domain6.xyz",
  "select_fields": ["id", "context"],
  "max_results": 8,
  "include_key_definition": true
}
```

*(Replace keys according to the provider's spec.)*

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Double‑Check

| ✅ Checkpoint | Why it matters |
|---------------|----------------|
| Authentication header present & valid | Prevents 401 Unauthorized errors. |
| Base URL correct | Avoid hitting sandbox vs production accidentally. |
| Field names exactly match the database schema | Typos cause empty result sets. |
| Pagination logic handled client‑side | If more than 8 matches exist, decide whether to page further. |

That’s all! Run one of the snippets above against your environment, tweak the auth/token bits, and you’ll receive a clean list of Object IDs plus their contextual descriptions—all wrapped inside a key‑definition envelope ready for consumption.
